DTREE-STOCH-VERIFY.text:
- [ ] **DTREE-STOCH-VERIFY** [code-then-inference] Tree verification at temperature > 0 by stochastic tree acceptance: SpecInfer/Sequoia-style multi-draft rejection over the token tree, where each child is tested against the residual distribution after its rejected siblings and the residual is resampled on full rejection, on the device top-K candidates.
      · note: tree verification at temp > 0 is NOT supported or validated today. All dtree work is greedy-only with an oracle gate, and SPEC-PIT.1 (the temp > 0 distribution gate) is still open.
      · done when: default-off knob commit with a CPU oracle test (exact residual-resample distribution over >= 640k draws) + SPEC-PIT.1 KS pass for the ON arm + verdict KEEP / DROP with paired tok/s CIs
      · model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 + DFlash2 tree draft, temp 1 / top-p 0.95 / top-k 20 · gate: SPEC-PIT.1, AK-GAP-1-STOCH-ACCEPT
      · stop rule: question = does stochastic tree acceptance beat chain stochastic accept in tok/s at identical output distribution? stop-on-answer: KS fail -> FAIL; e2e CI vs the chain arm clears 1.0084 either way from rep 4 (max 6); stop-on-futility: measured mean accepted length at temp 1 within 5% of the chain arm (no tree headroom)
      · region: gpu-q3 · est: code ~3 days; SPEC-PIT.1 run time + 5 interleaved e2e pairs, x1.25
      · code (done 2026-11-21): fork `llama.cpp-experimental-dtree-stoch-20261121` @ `7182434c3` (on 4a9ca940d / C17 1b83c6967), knob `LLAMA_DTREE_STOCH=1` (default off; temp > 0 batch-tree rounds only, temp <= 0 path unchanged). `common_sampler_sample_and_accept_tree` walks the tree from the anchor. At each node it runs the full sampler chain on that row (device top-K candidates when GGML_HIP_DEVICE_ACCEPT_STOCH is set) to get the target law p, then tries the distinct children in path order. Each child x is accepted with probability r(x)/sum(r), where r is p with every earlier rejected sibling zeroed. If all children are rejected, the walk draws from the final residual and stops; passing the last draft samples a bonus token. The drafter makes temp > 0 tree rounds point-mass: the main path is the greedy selector walk, the alternatives are its rank branches, and each draft carries a one-hot distribution, so a chain fallback stays exact too. Server: spec_tree_resolve runs the walk, which picks the winner (the lowest-index path consistent with the accepted tokens) and the accepted tokens in one pass; the accept path consumes them, using the pre-walk sampler clone as its checkpoint. SPEC-PIT.1 diagnostic: `LLAMA_SPEC_PIT_FILE=<path>` appends per-token `sum_smaller_probs p_token` from the chain and tree stochastic accept functions.
      · exactness: the drafts are fixed before the target is read, so each child is a point-mass proposal q = delta_x. For a point mass, rejection sampling accepts x with probability min(1, p(x)/q(x)) = p(x), and its residual is norm(max(p - q, 0)), which is p with x removed and renormalized. Applying that step to siblings in order is sampling without replacement. By induction over the siblings, P(emit y) = p(y) for every token y: a child is emitted at its own test, and any other token comes from the final residual. Conditioned on the emitted token, the walk continues in that child's subtree under the next row's law, so the joint law of the emitted sequence equals target sampling. The walk accepts with total probability sum over children of p(child), the same as sample-and-match. At temp 0 the walk is sample-and-match, i.e. the greedy longest match with the lowest path index, which is the existing tree path.
      · CPU test (`tests/test-dtree-stoch.cpp`, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, real 2-level tree: 2 siblings at depth 0 and 2 under c1): 640k walks on device top-32: chi-square p t1 0.879, t2|c1 0.369, t3|c1a 0.756, t2|c2 0.755; full-row path (30k): p 0.897 / 0.150 / 0.125 / 0.082. Emitted-length violations 0, same-seed stream mismatches 0, temp 0 bitwise equal to the existing tree path (greedy winner + accept_n) for 6/6 path orders. test-spec-dtree-paths OK (4800 cases). [no-belief: CPU oracle test, no served measurement]

The arms run in rotated quads: OFF/OFF2 = chain (4a9ca940d path), A = LLAMA_DTREE_STOCH=1 --draft-tree-mode batch --draft-tree-nodes auto (primary), T12 = the same at 12 nodes (reported). R23-48.text:
- [ ] **R23-48 — LEAVE-ONE-OUT ARM PER ACCUMULATED LEVER, run whenever the champion changes**
        (INF-70 finding relayed 2026-09-07 while run 29 was down). Verified: the loop A/Bs each NEW keep
        against the accumulated tip but never re-measures a PRIOR keep (`grep -rn "leave.one.out|re-?test|
        ablat" loop/` → nothing). INF-70 measured the failure this design hides: a lever that passed a
        26-arm study at +1.0% turned **−1.39%, sign-stable over 3 rounds**, after two later levers removed
        the stall it was paying for — *levers interact through what they remove*. GPU interaction classes
        differ (occupancy / bandwidth / launch overhead) but the shape is identical. Design: on each
        PROMOTE (champion-of-record advance) build one arm per accumulated keep with that keep reverted
        (`git revert --no-commit <keep>` in a detached worktree, incremental build via the object-digest
        path), paired A/B vs the champion at the calibrated floor; a keep whose removal is neutral-or-
        better is a candidate DROP (dropped keeps go to `experiments.md` as `retracted_by_loo` with the
        two sample vectors, never silently). Cost bound: n_keeps arms per promotion, not per iteration.
        Corollary already true here and to keep true: the headline is the assembled-stack A/B, never the
        product of solo deltas — the accumulator's `compounded_bench_pct` is a product ESTIMATE and must
        stay labelled as such on the dashboard (INF-70: product-of-solos predicted 1.50, measured 1.69;
        second stack sub-additive). Not applicable: page-cache eviction (models are VRAM-resident) and
        hot-server arm switching (reload is cheap on GPU). Evidence: `handoffs/active/cpu-decode-roofline-
        program.md` (CHAMP-2, SYNC-15), `wiki/benchmark-methodology.md` → *Measure the stack, not the parts*.
        · history: notes moved to autokernel-loop-box-history-20261122.md
